label: First lockdown
summary: Nationwide contact restrictions from 22-23 March 2020; shops, restaurants and schools closed. First easing from 15 April, with further steps in early May. The index starts in April, at its lowest point.

label: Second lockdown
summary: A partial lockdown from 2 November 2020 (restaurants and leisure closed), tightened to a hard lockdown in mid-December (non-essential shops closed). Eased in steps from March 2021.

label: Federal emergency brake
summary: A nationwide rule (Infektionsschutzgesetz §28b) tied restrictions and curfews to local infection rates, in force 23 April to 30 June 2021. Reopening followed through the early summer.

label: Omicron winter: 2G in shops
summary: Federal and state leaders agreed on 2 December 2021 that only vaccinated or recovered people could enter most shops (2G), in force from 4 December in most states, with several courts striking it down. Most nationwide measures ended in late March 2022.

label: Energy-price shock
summary: After the invasion of Ukraine, energy prices rose sharply: by October 2022 energy cost 43% more than a year earlier and German consumer-price inflation reached 10.4%, the highest in about 70 years.

label: Fuel-tax cut (Tankrabatt)
summary: Germany cut the tax on petrol by 35 cents a litre and on diesel by 17 cents for June to August 2022.

label: EUR 9 monthly transit ticket
summary: A EUR 9 a month ticket valid on all local and regional public transport in Germany, for June, July and August 2022.

label: Deutschlandticket launches (EUR 49)
summary: The EUR 49 a month national ticket for local and regional transport replaced the 9-euro ticket and has stayed on sale since.

label: Deutschlandticket rises to EUR 58
summary: The monthly price rose from EUR 49 to EUR 58 on 1 January 2025.

label: Deutschlandticket rises to EUR 63
summary: The monthly price rose from EUR 58 to EUR 63 on 1 January 2026; a further rise to EUR 66.80 is set for 2027.
source_title: The Local: EUR 63 Deutschlandticket locked in for 2026

label: Working from home stays higher
summary: Eurostat's labour-force survey shows people who usually work from home roughly doubling, from about 5% of employed people aged 15-64 in 2019 to about 9% in 2023 and 2024, with another 13% doing so sometimes. Fewer commuting days means fewer weekday parkers.
source_title: Eurostat, employed persons working from home (lfsa_ehomp)

label: More garages enter the sample
summary: Direct feeds for more cities started in August and September 2026 (Frankfurt, Hamburg, Freiburg and the Netherlands among them). Garages enter the year-on-year index only once they have a year of history, so these do not move the line yet.
